why_angle: The rival pages, and our own earlier version, repeat Anker's 1,600 W UltraFast figure and the 49-minute claim. None of them reads Anker's US nameplate of 120 V, 12 A max (1,440 W), which is also the code limit for one plug-in device on a standard 15 A circuit. None sets that against EcoFlow's 15 A rating or DJI's 13 A. This page checks each fast mode against what a US 120 V outlet can supply and shows the arithmetic, so it explains why the 49 minutes still fits under an hour at 120 V and why 1,200 W units can't.

page.title: Which 1,000 Wh power station charges fully from the wall in under an hour (2026)? Measured times, fast-mode conditions, wall watts
page.h1: Which 1,000 Wh portable power station fully charges from a wall outlet in under an hour? (2026)
page.desc: Measured 0–100 % wall-charge times for 1,000 Wh power stations, the fast mode each one needs, and what a US 120 V outlet allows: Anker rates the C1000 Gen 2's input at 12 A (1,440 W), not 1,600 W.
page.answer: Short answer. The fastest 1000 Wh power station that charges fully from the wall in under an hour is the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2: 0 to 100% AC in 49 minutes with UltraFast on, 47 min tested. On a US 120V outlet Anker rates it 12 A max (1,440 W), the limit for a standard 15 A circuit.
columns: Amps at 120 V (and the maker's rated limit)

cells.claim: 49 min, with UltraFast switched on in the Anker app and the standard Anker AC cable (Anker)
cells.measured: 47 min with UltraFast (The Technology Man, UK mains, about 20 °C; The Solar Lab); 1,097 Wh/hr average, peak just above 1,200 W, about 56 min in default mode (OutdoorGearLab)
cells.amps: 13.3 A at 1,600 W, but Anker's US rating is 120 V, 12 A max (1,440 W)

cells.measured: 50 min, no special mode named (OutdoorGearLab text; its spec table rounds to 0.9 h)
55 min (The Solar Lab); 1,180 Wh drawn from the wall per full charge (StorageReview)
cells.amps: 12.5 A; EcoFlow rates the US input 15 A, and StorageReview calls 1,500 W ideal on a 20 A circuit

cells.claim: 80 % in 45 min with TurboBoost; BLUETTI gives no 0–100 % AC time
cells.measured: 2.0 h at 512 Wh/hr, mode not stated (OutdoorGearLab)

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Anker's 49 minutes needs about 1,254 W into the battery on average: 1,024 Wh ÷ (49 ÷ 60 h) = 1,254 W.
  • At the wall it needs about 1,445 W. StorageReview metered 1,180 Wh from the wall to fill a 1,024 Wh DELTA 3 Plus, about 87 % efficient (1,024 ÷ 1,180 = 0.87). Using that as a stand-in for the Anker's same-size LFP pack: 1,180 Wh ÷ 0.817 h = 1,445 W. That is right at the 1,440 W Anker's 12 A rating allows (12 A × 120 V).
  • Held to 1,440 W, it is still under an hour: 49 min × 1,600 ÷ 1,440 = 54 min, if the draw stayed flat at the cap.
  • The DELTA 3 Plus averages about 1,264 W from the wall over its 56 minutes: 1,180 Wh ÷ (56 ÷ 60 h). Its 1,500 W peak is 12.5 A at 120 V (1,500 ÷ 120).
  • A 1,200 W input can't fill 1,024 Wh in under an hour once losses count: 1,180 Wh ÷ 1,200 W × 60 = 59 min, even with no slow-down near full. That is why BLUETTI claims only 80 % in 45 minutes for the Elite 100 V2.

What a US 120 V outlet lets each fast mode draw

Charge time depends on watts, and a US outlet limits watts through amps. The electrical code limits one cord-and-plug appliance to 80 % of its branch circuit (NEC 210.23(A)(1), as quoted by EC&M). On the standard 15 A household circuit that is 12 A, or 1,440 W at 120 V.

StationMaker's rated input at 120 VFast-mode charge wattsAmps those watts need
Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2120 V~, 12 A max (1,440 W)1,600 W UltraFast13.3 A
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus100–120 V~, 15 A (1,800 W), EcoFlow Team on Best Buy1,500 W12.5 A
DJI Power 1000 V2 (100–120 V model)100–120 V, 13 A max (1,560 W)DJI's spec page gives a current only13 A at most

Anker's US page prints "120V~ 12A Max" alongside "1,600W" UltraFast. Both can't hold at 120 V, so on a US outlet plan on about 1,440 W. That still covers the 49-minute claim, as the arithmetic above shows. Both 47-minute results had UltraFast on: The Technology Man tested on UK mains at about 20 °C with the supplied lead, and The Solar Lab does not give its voltage. OutdoorGearLab's US run averaged 1,097 Wh/hr and peaked just above 1,200 W, which matches the 1,200 W standard mode and about 56 minutes.

To get the 49 minutes: switch UltraFast on in the Anker app, use Anker's standard AC cable (Anker warns that third-party cables may cause damage), charge within its 32–104 °F range, and keep heavy loads off the same circuit.

On the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, StorageReview saw 1.45 kW in the app. It says 1,500 W is ideal on a 20 A receptacle and circuit, and that the app's charge-speed limit is there for 15 A, 120 V plugs. Lowering that limit on a shared 15 A circuit will push the charge past its 55–56 minutes. DJI rates its 100–120 V Power 1000 V2 at 13 A, and OutdoorGearLab timed it at 59 minutes, just inside the hour.

Not recommended

The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is often listed as an under-an-hour unit, but OutdoorGearLab measured only 563 Wh/hr. That is almost 2 hours to refill its 1,070 Wh. The reviewers note that many competitors in the class charge fully in under an hour, and the review doesn't name the charging mode used. If a full charge within the hour is the reason you're buying, choose one of the stations above.
